title.narrative: Design support - Cultural and Creative Industries in Kosovo
Designstöd - Kulturella and kreativa näringar i Kosovo

description.narrative: Målen för själva insatsen är: 1) Underlag till Kulturministeriet för en nationell strategi för kulturella kreativa näringar. Beslut om insats Decision on Contribution Enhet/Amb.beslut Unit/Emb. Decision Contribution ID: 16649 3 (15) 2) Ett starkt utvecklat partnerskap och en plattform för de kulturella och kreativa sektorerna i Kosovo. 2) En testad verksamhet och pilot där bland annat animation och film höjer värdet, kunskapen och användandet av Kosovos kulturarv. 3) Ett nytt programförslag inom kulturella kreativa näringar som syftar till att stärka Kosovos roll inom området vilket ska generera arbete, ökad inkluderande ekonomisk utveckling samt bidra till ett fredligt samhälle.

The goals of the effort itself are: 1) Background papers to the Ministry of culture, Youth and Sports as input to the national strategy for cultural creative industries with links to European networks. 2) A strong developed partnership and platform for the cultural and creative sectors in Kosovo. 3) A tested pilot where, among other things, animation and film increase the value, knowledge and use of Kosovo's cultural heritage. 4) A new program proposal with many other actors and stakeholders in cultural creative industries to strengthen Kosovo's role in the area, which may generate work, increased inclusive economic development and contribute to a peaceful society.

Vision The overall vision is to strengthen cultural creative sectors and industries in Kosovo where many initiatives contribute to a peaceful inclusive society, as well as generating jobs and increased economic growth. title.narrative: Grant arrangement between Sida and Lund University
Decision on contribution - Design support Cultural Creative Industries in Kosovo

description.narrative:
In the beginning of the project Tu Pa Tu Ba, the team structured their work into five phases. The goals were a bit modified during the work, but it was still aiming for the same outcomes. Examples of the results are therefore shortly described under the initial goal areas.
1) Background papers to the Ministry of culture, Youth and Sports as input to the national strategy for cultural creative industries with links to European networks.
One of the reasons this project started, was that the Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sports, had met the representatives from Lund University and Future By Lund during Manifesta 2022. A mutual understanding and interest was born and as Cultural Creative Industries was seen by the government as an area to invest in, Kosovo's ministry asked the Swedish partners for a collaboration on a policy level. The government was about to conduct a strategy for the area. After a lot of brain storming and dialogue, and after Sida's decision on the contribution, the partners from Lund decided to contribute to the strategy. However, they did not write the government's policy paper, which was partly asked for - they gave input in how to work strategically and with an innovative portfolio approach. This contribution from Lund to the government was stated in workshops, dialogue and also a document attached here in TRAC. The government of Kosovo involved other consultants for writting the main policy document / CCI-strategy, and the writting was coordinated partly by UNDP and supported financially by the Britsh Council. However, the strategy is yet not finalized due to the challenges of forming a new government in Kosovo, following the February 2025 elections.
Except from this concrete input to the strategy, the mutual interest for the Cultural Creative Industries in Kosovo and whole Europe, also resulted in a good relation. Further ahead Kosovo could benefit from the European Network for CCI, Ekip, which is lead by Lund University with support from the EU commission. This European platform for cultural workers, organizations and innovators has opened an opportunity to further develop and for Kosovo as a country, being in the front line working in CCI-sector and representing not only itself, but also Western Balkan. An unexpected result has been that actors within the cultural sector in Kosovo have already connected to ekip partners in Europe, and into broader collaborations, according to Lund University.
2) A strong developed partnership and platform for the cultural and creative sectors in Kosovo.
When this project started in January 2024, the Swedish team had already initiated an exchange with Anibar and UN-Habitat, parallel to having a dialogue with the Kosovo government. During Manifesta, in 2022, the Swedish partner had met with the government and in 2023 Lund University travelled to Kosovo to continue planning a potential project and eventual partnerships within the Cultural Creative Industry - area. The Embassy of Sweden/Sida facilitated, during the autumn 2023, a meeting with UN-Habit who in return arranged visits in Pristina, and in Peja, where Lund University met with the municipalities, the organizations 7Arte and Anibar. In return these actors had connections to other stakeholder that later on benefited the progress of the project and who expended the network for Lund University. It was during autumn 2023 that Lund University applied for a design support.
A concrete platform, meaning physically on site, for the cultural and creative sector is not there. However, the network within the sector is assessed to have been strengthened. Thanks to the Swedish initiative the interest has also increased from the donor community. After a round-table dialogue at the Embassy of Sweden, the project team continued the discussion on how the international community together with the actors in Kosovo could strengthen the CCI-sector. Currently an exchange is mainly taken place between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, The Embassy of France and UNDP. They all express their recognition of the relevance and importance of an innovation platform for the Cultural and Creative Industries in Kosovo - together with the Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sport. Even other ministries expressed their interest in an overall strategy for the CCI-sector.
During the project several workshops and education sessions took place in both Kosovo and Sweden in methods for a innovative portfolio approach- with special expertise from Sweden. The method is similar to working according to a system analysis and its core has to to with a holistic view where actors can connected to other actors in developing a project, business or a like.
As the team from the project visited Sweden, new relations were established which strengthened the mutual interest between Kosovo and Sweden further. For instance, through the ekip-event, on June 4 this year (Unexpected Arts and Science Innovation Forum) the partners in the project learnt from not only the latest research on innovation opportunities and challenges in AI/Immerse Tech, Fashion, Craft, Platformisation of Music, and Performing Arts etc. They also connected with a wide network of experts and stakeholders on CCI innovation across Europe.
The knowledge, methods and connections with others fed into the pilot projects and further plans of collaboration.
3) A tested pilot where, among other things, animation and film increase the value, knowledge and use of Kosovo's cultural heritage.
After all the planning, learning and structuring, the project started developing a pilot - using the innovative portfolio approach. It resulted in three different pilots:
1) A demo app prototype for Prishtinas Old Bazaar inspired by the BeHereThen concept (based in Sweden). This app was the first of its kind for Kosovo, with integrated geographic location, historical photos, and animations to narrate the cultural and historical significance of the bazaar. Conducted content and image selection, digitization, and rights acquisition for materials to be used in the app. The launch was noticed by the media, and a long feature was sent at the national TV - stressing that the app can be used for a long term by the public, schools, tourists and a like.
2) The Vushtrri Courthouse case with an innovative use of the augmented reality (AR) and repurpose cultural and architectural heritage. Thanks to interviews, a well kept database with documented descriptions of the courthouse in Vushtrri, the team projected a historical animated film on the wall - outdoor - about the house. The purpose was to raise awareness of the value of the building and to question the public and different actors how the courthouse could be used. Currently there are businesses who show interest in investing in the house and the municipality considers it to be a cultural centre or art hall. This case served as a pilot for the broader goal of repurposing historic buildings across Kosovo. By integrating digital storytelling with immerse visual experiences, the project highlights how heritage sites can evolve into vibrant cultural spaces that resonate with contemporary audiences.
3) The Roman Archaeology and Digital Scanning portfolio case focuses on the ancient Roman city of Municipium DD in Socanica, within the Leposavic Municipality. This third pilot is more in a planning stage - compared to the other two. The idea is to utilize advanced scanning technologies to reimagine and visualize this significant archaeological site to present the historical richness of the area, creating an immerse experience that highlights its cultural and historical value and potential economic growth thanks to tourism or a like. The initiative emphasizes the potential of Municipium DD to become a cornerstone for tourism and income, reconciliation, and community engagement.
Within this case, students at Lund university and archaeologists have expressed their interest to have a collaboration - with the goal to developing the roman site into something consisting for Kosovo, its citizens and tourists. The project team stresses that this case should be developed with the purpose to integrate a peace perspective.
4) A new program proposal with many other actors and stakeholders in cultural creative industries to strengthen Kosovo's role in the area, which may generate job opportunities, increased inclusive economic development and contribute to a peaceful society.
Lund University and its partners have, after workshops and joint efforts, designed a new program proposal for the establishment of a future innovation platform: Future by Kosovo. The project team stresses that the members of the group have developed a strong and diverse partnership that now understands and have "the capacity to work with a portfolio approach, as a way of collaborating for innovation with the Cultural and Creative Sectors and Industries", as written in the final report. There is an informal network with around 25 organizations that have potential to be more formalized and structured, to be able to form a hub or platform at site. The project team has also discussed a potential to have three hubs - in three cities.
The team has built on what they achieved during the design phase, and would like to develop the cross-innovation area cultural heritage/immersive tech/animation so that the methods can be used within other CCI cross-innovation areas. The project is ending, but it has already inspired municipalities to start discussing potential areas to develop, things that are already on-going in a smaller scale and that have potential to be scaled up. For instance; Creative Sparks initiative in Mitrovica, ideas of how to develop costumes collection in Zym or music festivals with digital - and green-tech as an innovation portfolio.
